NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG.name: GDP growth (annual %)
NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG.description: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. This indicator denotes the percentage change over each previous year of the constant price (base year 2015) series in United States dollars.

FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.name: Inflation, consumer prices (annual %)
FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.description: Inflation as measured by the consumer price index reflects the annual percentage change in the cost to the average consumer of acquiring a basket of goods and services that may be fixed or changed at specified intervals, such as yearly.
FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG.sourceOrganization: International Financial Statistics database, International Monetary Fund (IMF)

notes: G20 country coverage is19 sovereign countries. The European Union and African Union are additional G20 members and are not silently treated as countries or replaced with euro-area values.
No2026 annual GDP or annual CPI rows were returned by the World Bank API. Those positions are explicitnulls, not forecasts or zeroes.
Historical World Bank observations may contain statistical estimates and revisions. They are reported historical series; no forecast dataset has been mixed in.
Latest CPI observations use different reference months and national coverage. Some October figures and India September are provisional estimates of an observed period, clearly labelled.
Annual inflation history and a monthly year-on-year CPI print are different summaries. Do not join them into one continuous annual-change series without clear frequency labels.
A low or high growth/inflation observation alone is not a complete judgement of a country’s economic health.

These are each country's own headline CPI series. Baskets, population coverage, weights, housing treatment, reference bases and compilation methods differ, so the figures are not a harmonised international index.
The latest reference month differs by country. September and October observations must retain their visible period labels; avoid presenting their ordering as a like-for-like ranking.
Germany, France and Italy use national CPI here rather than the EU Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP).
A false provisional flag means that the cited release did not label the headline observation preliminary or provisional; it does not guarantee that statistical revisions are impossible.

Saudi Arabia's official dashboard verifies the value and reference month, but the original release date could not be verified directly and is null. The dashboard's retrieval date must not be presented as its release date.
This file covers the 19 G20 sovereign country members; the European Union and African Union are not separate country observations.
meta.monthlySelectionPolicy: Latest complete-month national headline consumer-price inflation available from the cited official sources by 3 November 2026. October statistical flash estimates are included only with an explicit provisional flag. Mexico's October fortnightly observation is excluded because it is not a complete calendar month. No forecasts are included.
